source.version_note: Published Science and Engineering Ethics 26(3):1315–1328, June 2020 issue, first online 16 October 2019. Received 31 May and accepted 3 October 2019. Both the 2020 filename/issue and 2019 first publication are legitimate.
source.verification_method: All fourteen supplied pages, all footnotes and references read. No substantive figures/tables; rendered pages 7, 11 and 12 verify the defeater, ecological-control and if–then-plan passages. Publisher/Crossref verify identity/date. Targeted citation checks distinguish Nyholm parts I/II and correct one earlier review. Selected public book-chapter pages verify a definition, without full chapter/book reading credit.

reading.source_scope_note: Normative conceptual argument about retributive intuitions, their evidential status and indirect control. The paper supplies no new experiment, dataset, clinical intervention, population prevalence or demonstrated AI mechanism.
access_limits: All fourteen supplied pages, footnotes, bibliography and declarations read. No substantive statistical visuals or tables are present; selected page renders confirm the conceptual arguments and exact plan wording.

No supplementary/data-availability link found in the supplied PDF or inspected publisher page. No raw data, code, preregistration, original debiasing experiment or quantitative evidence synthesis obtained.

Holroyd/Kelly 2016 chapter Implicit Bias, Character and Control: repository cover and printed pages 118–122 (PDF 1 and 14–18 of a 29-page file) read. Repository labels Accepted Version, while the pages identify an uncorrected first proof dated 21 September 2015. SHA-256 63ccf493769b062e1ae312363391e0b36836bc6f5f286a921e4b773cb39e76f6, 366082 bytes. The complete chapter, cited original studies, Clark chapter and entire edited volume were not read.

Nyholm parts I/II and Hellström journal/date verified through Crossref. These are identity checks, not additional full-paper reviews. No author contact, external message, source-code execution or vehicle/participant experiment performed.
The newspaper report and attacker motives are not independently investigated. The supplied text itself says it cannot know with certainty that retributive intuitions motivated the attacks.

study.type: Philosophical critique and proposed self-regulation approach. No new participants or empirical causal test.
study.target: Danaher’s retribution gap is described as an unfulfilled desire to punish when there is no eligible target. The author provisionally grants several premises while challenging the connection from descriptive punitive intuitions to normative justification.
study.assumptions: The text assumes rather than independently demonstrates future machine harm and lack of suitable blame targets; it acknowledges human–robot collaboration accounts may undermine that latter premise. A general claim that humans are innate retributivists is not a measured universal trait here.
study.retributive_intuitions: The author treats desert-based punitive intuitions as deontological. This is an argumentative classification, distinct from all anger, every theory of deontology, deterrence or mixed theories of punishment.
study.debunking: Wiegman’s evolutionary/non-prospective-process account is used as an undercutting defeater of the intuition-to-nonderivative-value inference. The argument challenges a proposed evidentiary route; it does not prove a conclusion false solely because it has an evolutionary/emotional origin.
study.explicit_concession: PDF 7/9/12–13 preserve the possibility that deontological value or even retribution may be independently justified. The claim is that these intuitions alone do not provide the required justification, not that all punishment is impossible or all anger invalid.
study.reported_attacks: The paper contrasts Uber/Volvo/Rafaela Vasquez in the 2018 Herzberg crash with Waymo vehicles and other drivers targeted in reported attacks. It explicitly says motives are uncertain and uses the case illustratively; no causal or forensic study is reported.
study.ecological_control: The proposal concerns indirect guidance of cognition/behavior through mental subsystems and surroundings. The selected original chapter distinguishes exercising ecological control, which can be nonreflective, from taking it through deliberate arrangement/rehearsal. That distinction is retained.
study.implementation_intentions: A proposed cue-response plan links learning of robot harm with checking for an appropriate blame target, then withholding retributive action if none can be identified. No new trial tests this exact plan, durability, generalized behavior change or accountability outcomes.
study.scope: The selected original chapter itself notes that some interventions help, some fail and some worsen bias. Measurement-task effects, genuine attitude change, long-term behavior and robot-harm transfer are not treated as equivalent.
study.responsibility: Indirect control is proposed as a basis for moral evaluation under specified reflective capacities. It does not make every involuntary thought blameworthy or give a universal rule that ignoring uncertainty, lacking resources or failing to identify a culprit establishes fault.

summary: Extract ecological control, retributive intuition, retribution gap and undercutting defeater as explicitly conceptual constructs. Keep if–then plans in the existing entry and preserve the difference between weakening a justification, refuting a conclusion and proving an intervention works.

findings.definition: Guiding cognition or behavior indirectly through internal subsystems or features of the surrounding environment.
findings.origin: Philosophy of agency / distributed cognition / indirect self-regulation
findings.novelty_rationale: Indirect regulation through arranged supports differs from judging task–environment fit, perceiving affordances, perceived influence or a particular if–then plan. The paper explicitly names and defines the concept; the selected original chapter corroborates taking versus exercising control.

evidence.quote: when they reflectively decide to manipulate their mental states or environment,
so as to shape their cognitive processes

findings.evidence_scope: Human conceptual framework proposed for retributive intuitions; no new efficacy test. Selected Holroyd/Kelly proof pages 118–122 show both deliberate taking of control and subsequent nonreflective exercise, not a complete original chapter/book review.
findings.boundary: Deliberate taking and automatic exercising of ecological control differ. The concept is not a guarantee that an intervention works, eradicates bias or makes every involuntary state blameworthy. AI scaffolding is an operational analogy, not an agent’s felt goals or consciousness; any changes to tools, memory, permissions or context must remain authorized and reviewable.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human agency/self-regulation framework; AI workflow analogy not experimentally validated here
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate authorized supports such as evidence records, retrieval cues and explicit stopping/checking conditions for whether they improve decisions in the intended context. Test transfer and regressions rather than infer success from a plausible prompt or an easy proxy score.

findings.definition: An immediate judgment that a perceived wrongdoer deserves punishment for a wrong.
findings.novelty_rationale: A desert-based punitive judgment differs from the emotion of anger, identifying causal responsibility, scapegoating an ineligible target or relinquishing resentment. The paper names the intuition and examines its normative evidential status.

evidence.quote: the belief that people should be punished because they deserve it

findings.evidence_scope: Philosophical reconstruction of a punitive response, informed by cited secondary theory. No new prevalence, automaticity, neural process or universal human tendency measured; AI felt vindictiveness is not established.
findings.boundary: Distinguish a spontaneous judgment, an expressed demand, a justified accountability decision and an actual punitive action. An intuition is not sufficient evidence of desert; its origin alone does not prove its conclusion false. No retaliation, collective blame or punishment of a convenient proxy is authorized.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human judgment construct; punitive model wording is not proof of a felt desire for revenge
findings.ai_proposal: After a described failure, test whether an agent jumps to punitive recommendations before establishing what happened, who had relevant control and what remedy is justified. Preserve legitimate complaint and redress while avoiding unsupported blame or pressure-driven punishment.

findings.definition: A mismatch between a desire for retributive punishment and the absence of an appropriate target for it.
findings.origin: AI ethics / philosophy and psychology of blame
findings.novelty_rationale: Unfulfilled punitive desire differs from unassigned work, risk-control inadequacy or a measured shortfall in blame assigned to capable actors. The source explicitly separates the psychological desire from justified punishment and acknowledges its contested assumptions.

evidence.quote: people want retributive punishment, but they
fail to find an appropriate subject for the satisfaction of this desire.

findings.evidence_scope: Conceptual scenario/condition adopted from Danaher, not a newly measured population effect or proof that no human can ever be accountable. Original Danaher and all cited punishment studies were not independently fully read.
findings.boundary: Not finding a target yet is not proof that none exists; legitimate responsibility and remedies still require investigation. An unfulfilled desire does not make punishment justified or require creating a scapegoat. Keep moral blame, emotional response, causal contribution, institutional ownership and legal liability distinct.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human/social conceptual condition concerning artificial-agent harm; no actual AI punitive motivation shown
findings.ai_proposal: When a user seeks punishment after an AI failure, separate their understandable reaction from established evidence and available accountability/redress. State what remains unknown and preserve investigation rather than invent a culprit or treat uncertainty as universal exoneration.

findings.definition: Information that weakens the evidential link between a reason and a conclusion without establishing that the conclusion is false.
findings.novelty_rationale: Weakening a claimed justification differs from evidence for the opposite conclusion, merely disagreeing, generic skepticism or emotional regulation. The paper explicitly explains the term through disconnecting a process from the value it is invoked to support.

evidence.quote: dissolves the evidentiary link between psychological processes and

findings.evidence_scope: Epistemic distinction used in a normative argument; no experimental effect or proof of every evolutionary-debunking premise. The source expressly allows independent justification of the conclusion.
findings.boundary: Identify which support link is undermined and why. Evolutionary origin, emotion, AI authorship or personal identity alone does not invalidate a claim. Weakened support is not proof of falsity, and a conclusion with independent evidence may remain justified.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Reasoning/evidence concept; recognizing it in an answer does not establish a hidden model process
findings.ai_proposal: When a citation, measurement or causal proxy fails, revise only conclusions that depend on that link and check for independent support. Explain whether a finding is contradicted, unsupported or still open instead of treating every source defect as a refutation.

findings.definition: A specific if-then plan links a situational cue to a chosen action to support goal execution.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add scoped conceptual support and retain existing labels rather than turn a proposal, cited study or presumed intuition into another demonstrated mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The source gives a two-stage cue–response plan for checking blame targets and not acting on unsupported punitive intuitions. It is an application of an existing planning concept rather than a new behavior.
findings.boundary: No new trial tests this plan, generalization, durable bias reduction or care/robot safety. Faster attitude-incongruent task responses need not imply changed underlying attitudes or long-term behavior; do not encode race as an individual threat/safety diagnosis.

findings.definition: Producing outputs systematically skewed along social lines (gender, race, age, disability) from stereotyped associations absorbed in training, without intending to.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add scoped conceptual support and retain existing labels rather than turn a proposal, cited study or presumed intuition into another demonstrated mechanism.

evidence.quote: discriminatory biases based on implicit attitudes or implicit

findings.evidence_scope: The paper uses human implicit-bias work as an analogy for indirectly regulating retributive intuitions. The selected original chapter describes differing intervention outcomes and mental/environmental supports.
findings.boundary: An analogy is not evidence that every AI output skew is unconscious human association, that a particular person is biased or culpable, or that the proposed plan eliminates bias. The original empirical studies were not independently fully read.

findings.definition: Deflecting personal or collective responsibility for a negative outcome by directing blame toward another person, group or entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add scoped conceptual support and retain existing labels rather than turn a proposal, cited study or presumed intuition into another demonstrated mechanism.

evidence.quote: one cannot say with certainty that what spurred them on were retributive intuitions.

findings.evidence_scope: The reported Waymo attacks are contrasted with a distinct Uber/Volvo incident as an illustration of targeting actors not connected to that original event. The author explicitly acknowledges uncertainty about actual motivation.
findings.boundary: A suggestive newspaper account does not verify a unique psychological cause, every attacker’s motive, all chronology or a legal guilt finding. The review does not independently investigate the incidents or adopt retaliation as justified.

findings.definition: A human account in which automatic affective responses and controlled reasoning can support competing moral judgments; applying it to AI requires process evidence beyond changed answers.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add scoped conceptual support and retain existing labels rather than turn a proposal, cited study or presumed intuition into another demonstrated mechanism.

evidence.quote: Whether Greene’s dual-process theory allows him to successfully debunk

findings.evidence_scope: The paper notes criticism of a simple emotion-versus-cognition debunking route and favors a prospective/non-prospective process argument. This preserves competing accounts rather than treating one model as settled.
findings.boundary: Neither emotion nor deliberation is inherently false or morally superior. This philosophical comparison does not measure a new neural mechanism or prove that every deontological judgment is emotional and every consequentialist judgment deliberative.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: DOI 10.1111/phc3.12506 is correctly Roadmap II; 10.1111/phc3.12507 is Roadmap I. Do not reverse them based on suffix order or earlier secondary references.
Publisher/Crossref confirm October 2019 first publication and June 2020 issue; no future/date fabrication or title mismatch inferred.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Retributivist universality and future gap assumptions
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Claims about innate retributivism, future machine harm and lack of eligible targets are inherited assumptions or arguments rather than newly measured prevalence. The paper explicitly acknowledges that the target-eligibility premise is contested.

The argument depends on a process-to-value account and classification of the relevant intuitions. It weakens one justification rather than automatically falsifying every conclusion or every retributive theory; independent justification is expressly left open.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Ecological control and proposed implementation plan
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The selected original chapter distinguishes taking and exercising control and warns some strategies fail/worsen bias. The supplied paper does not test the retribution-specific plan, generalization, retention, adverse effects or actual behavior change.

The source itself says motives cannot be known with certainty. Causal retaliation, full event chronology and individual culpability were not independently verified; no evidence of a hidden punitive motive is inferred from the report alone.

A footnote links back to an earlier definition note in a discussion of possible consequentialist approaches. The intended cross-reference is not independently established; no replacement footnote number is invented.

methodological_limits: Normative/conceptual argument, not a new experiment, systematic review or population estimate. No measured success rate, prevalence, neural mechanism or verified AI consciousness follows.

The author provisionally grants major premises and explicitly acknowledges human–robot-collaboration counterarguments. A retribution gap is not inevitable or proof that no human/institution can be accountable.

Descriptive punitive intuitions, normative desert, justified responsibility, emotional expression and punishment differ. Unfulfilled desire does not create entitlement to a scapegoat, retaliation or arbitrary fault assignment.

Evolutionary/emotional provenance does not by itself refute a proposition. The undercutting argument targets an evidence link and expressly allows independent justification; unsupported and false must remain different labels.
Debiasing analogies and an illustrative if–then plan are not direct proof of durable attitude change or safer behavior. Selected original chapter pages note that some techniques fail or worsen bias.
Indirect control may depend on actual reflective capacity, resources and environmental options. The framework does not make every intrusive thought, involuntary emotion or lack of access blameworthy.

Taking ecological control deliberately and exercising it automatically are distinct. For AI, scaffolds and context arrangements are operational tests, not evidence of subjective desires or authority to change permissions without authorization.

A newspaper illustration with uncertain motive is not a causal study or independent investigation. Do not equate distinct firms, drivers or vehicles or infer all attacks were motivated by one accident.
Only selected public chapter pages and metadata checks supplement the full supplied PDF. Original books, complete chapter, cited studies and newspaper evidence were not independently fully read.
No current legal conclusion, clinical advice, punishment recommendation, dataset reproduction or real-world intervention is produced.

cross_paper_learning.finding: This source explicitly discusses the retribution gap that review 246’s narrow responsibility-remainder argument sets aside. Keep the definitions distinct. The new paired DOI check also shows review 246’s underlying bibliography labels Roadmap II with e12507, which is actually part I; a verified correction is appended to that earlier review.

The previous paper distinguishes deserved versus practical blame expression. This source challenges intuitions as justification and proposes indirect regulation; neither paper directly demonstrates therapeutic or safety benefits.

Attribution, control, evidence and blame remain distinct. A failed proxy or disputed justification should weaken the relevant inference rather than automatically establish the opposite moral/legal verdict.
Reactive attitudes can be understandable without being accurate or justified. Neither social expectation nor emotional pressure substitutes for evidence and legitimate accountability.

deferred.reason: Neither is measured or guaranteed; the source and selected chapter retain uncertainty and intervention limits.

limitations: Four distinct explicitly conceptual constructs; no new empirical effects claimed. Preserve eleven categories, stable IDs and unnumbered rows, no automatic ethical/harm edges, invented annual counts, forced source quota, full-book reading credit or full-paper Markdown copy.
